evidence.label: Contact Fano manifolds and the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture

headline: Contact Fano manifolds are homogeneous, which settles the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture on quaternionic-Kähler spaces.
scope: Complex projective contact Fano manifolds of dimension at least three; positive quaternionic-Kähler manifolds of real dimension at least eight.
plain: A contact structure is a field of maximally twisted hyperplanes on an odd-dimensional manifold. The paper claims every smooth projective contact Fano manifold is on a known list built from simple Lie algebras. A corollary is the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture. Every closed positive quaternionic-Kähler manifold of real dimension at least eight would be a symmetric Wolf space, up to scale. The paper also claims a classification of all projective contact manifolds.
doesNot: This does not cover quaternionic-Kähler manifolds with negative or zero scalar curvature, or real dimension four.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: C. LeBrun and S. Salamon, strong rigidity of positive quaternion-Kähler manifolds
scorecard.significanceWhy: If correct, it settles a decades-old classification problem linking complex contact geometry and Riemannian holonomy.

explanation:
Take ordinary three-dimensional space with coordinates x, y and z. Consider the one-form α = dz − y dx. At each point it picks out a plane of directions, the ones on which α is zero. Its derivative is dα = dx ∧ dy. Then α ∧ dα = dz ∧ dx ∧ dy, which is never zero. That is exactly the condition for a contact structure[1]. The planes twist so much that no surface is tangent to all of them, even locally.

On a complex manifold of odd dimension 2n + 1, a contact structure is such a field of hyperplanes. A contact Fano manifold is a compact projective one whose anticanonical bundle is ample, a strong positivity condition. There is a family of standard examples. Each simple complex Lie algebra, an algebra of infinitesimal symmetries, has a closed adjoint orbit. Projectivized, it gives the adjoint variety, with a canonical contact structure[2]. For example, three-dimensional projective space arises from the symplectic Lie algebra of 4 × 4 matrices[3].

The contact-Fano homogeneity conjecture says these are the only examples. This paper claims to prove it[4]. Every smooth connected complex projective contact Fano manifold of dimension at least three is one of these adjoint varieties[5]. The match also carries the given contact structure to the canonical one[5].

The second payoff is in Riemannian geometry. A quaternionic-Kähler manifold has real dimension 4m and a metric whose holonomy lies in the group Sp(m)Sp(1)[6]. Holonomy records how directions turn when carried around loops. Positive means positive scalar curvature, a kind of average curvature. The compact symmetric examples are called Wolf spaces[6]. The LeBrun–Salamon conjecture concerns the case m ≥ 2. It says every closed positive quaternionic-Kähler manifold is a Wolf space up to scale. The paper claims to prove this as a corollary[7,8]. For m = 2 the real dimension is 8.

The link is the twistor space. Each such manifold of real dimension 4m has a twistor space, a two-sphere bundle over it. Its real dimension is 4m + 2, so its complex dimension is 2m + 1. Salamon showed this twistor space is a contact Fano manifold[9]. So the algebraic theorem applies to it[8]. From the twistor space the paper then recovers the original metric[8].

What was known before? Poon and Salamon settled real dimension eight[10]. Buczyński and Wiśniewski settled real dimensions twelve and sixteen[11]. Several results needed extra hypotheses, such as a reductive symmetry group[12]. Brendle and Semmelmann proved symmetry under nonnegative sectional curvature[13]. Earlier preprints by Kobayashi and Yasukura claimed broad classifications. Later comments by Yasukura identified errors in two of his versions[14].

The obstacle is to find enough symmetries. The paper must build global vector fields that preserve the contact structure and span every tangent space[15]. It does this with contact lines, the simplest rational curves in the manifold. Two such lines are joined and smoothed into a conic[16]. The paper builds a symmetric section on pairs of points whose behaviour near the diagonal forces the fields to span[17]. Then the symmetry group acts transitively, and the manifold is homogeneous.

The paper also claims a classification of all projective contact manifolds of dimension at least three. With second Betti number 1, they are adjoint varieties[18]. With second Betti number at least 2, the manifold is the projectivized cotangent bundle of a smooth projective variety[18].

How sure is this? No Lean formalization is listed for this paper in the openai/math release. So no computer proof checker has checked it. No specialist review has been published.
hypeCheck: Major only if the proof holds. Earlier claimed proofs of this classification were later found to contain errors. No Lean formalization is listed and no specialist review is published.

glossary.meaning: A field of hyperplanes that twists so much that no hypersurface is tangent to all of them.
